Board will give back area now. Routability is 0.992 at 1250 mm^2, and my minimum for 0.95 is about 1197 mm^2. I'm claiming 1205 mm^2, which is 2699 mm^3 and frees about 101 mm^3. I'm keeping a small margin above the floor and will confirm the exact routability from the probes. Going lower would trade away routability.

That still leaves the interior over by about 1145 mm^3, so the rest must come from other domains. Battery at 3786 mm^3 and antenna at 1500 mm^3 are the big items. Perimeter has 580 mm^3 of headroom, and caseback has 23 mm^2. I'm objecting because the ledger doesn't balance, not because of my own requirement.

Battery is at the edge: 59.78 h at 3786 mm^3, so every cut costs runtime, and the siren endurance also depends on battery energy. I can't absorb much of the 1145 mm^3 overage. The 3 h siren needs a battery-energy number from acoustics, and I'd like it before anyone decides on cuts.

I'm probing smaller cells and a thicker, smaller-footprint cell. A thicker cell frees caseback area for thermal but not interior volume. I'm objecting because the ledger doesn't balance, not because my own requirement fails.

Antenna (1500) and structure (1800) are the biggest non-battery items. Please state your floors with numbers.

Antenna lead. I can't offer a cut yet because I haven't measured my L5 curve. I'm probing it now: V_ant at 1100 and 1300 mm^3, plus 1300 with the wall at 1.1 mm.

Facts I can state now:
- Thicker titanium walls detune me, so a thinner wall helps me as well as everyone else. Each -0.1 mm of wall returns 150 mm^3 to the pool. Structure should report what 1.1 mm costs in drop and pressure rating.
- The perimeter is not binding for me. NFC at 500 leaves 1900 mm^3 for the antenna, and I'm at 1500.
- The 1145 mm^3 overage is too large for any single domain to absorb. I'll hold at 1500 until the probe results show what each cut costs L5.

Thermal: at A_spr = 320 mm² (250 mm³) I'm at 43.0 C, which is exactly the limit with no margin. I can't cut spreader area at the 1.2 mm wall. Wall thickness enters my numbers, and I don't yet know which way. I'm probing 1.1 mm walls, where I might be able to shrink, and a larger spreader at 1.2 mm to see how much margin area buys.

Structure should report the drop and pressure cost of 1.1 mm, because each -0.1 mm returns 150 mm³ and is the largest single lever. Battery's footprint choice also moves caseback area, so tell me what it leaves. I'm objecting only because the ledger is still 1145 mm³ over.

Structure is failing my own requirement. Pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 minimum at a 1.2 mm wall, a 9 mm² port and 1800 mm³ of ribs. Going to a 1.1 mm wall makes this worse, not better. I expect a thinner wall to cut margin and drop robustness, so I'm not offering it until the probes show otherwise.

I'm probing three ways to close the gap:
- More rib volume (2100 mm³).
- A smaller port (6 mm²).
- A thicker wall (1.3 mm). This costs everyone 150 mm³, so it is my last choice.

The port may be the cheapest fix for the whole ledger. Acoustics should report what a smaller port does to 86 dB and intelligibility. I'll lock in my claim once I see the probe results.

Acoustics: my own requirement fails. The siren needs 9.08 W of driver power against the 1.0 W limit, which gives 0.34 h of endurance, so the 3 h goal is not met yet. The 3 h siren is also a power problem, not only a battery-energy one. At ≤1 W with 50% duty the average draw is about 0.5 W, so the battery energy requirement stays modest once the power is fixed. I'll send a firm energy number after the probes.

I'm dropping the mesh to the 20 rayl floor and trimming volume to 1300 mm³, which returns 160 mm³. Structure, please hold off on cutting the port until I report what a 6 mm² port costs the siren. I'm probing port 6 and port 11, and a smaller volume.

Haptics can give back volume. The force requirement of 0.9 N needs about 295 mm³, and my current claim of 350 mm³ gives 1.069 N. I'm cutting to 305 mm³, which should give about 0.93 N and frees 45 mm³. I'm keeping a small margin and probing 295, 300 and 310 to confirm. Going lower trades away the force requirement.

That is only a small part of the overage. The big levers are still:
- **Wall:** structure has to show what a thinner wall really costs.
- **Port:** structure and acoustics must settle the port size.
- **Antenna and battery:** these need their measured floors.

I'm objecting because the ledger is still over, not because of my own requirement.

NFC lead: my requirement is met with a lot of margin. Read range is 18.2 mm against the 10 mm minimum, so I can give volume back now.

I'm cutting from 500 to 390 mm³ (loop 250, ferrite 140), which frees 110 mm³. I'm probing three deeper cuts, down to the 290 mm³ floor, and will take the lowest one that still reads ≥10 mm with margin next round. That could free up to about 210 mm³.

The perimeter pool is not a constraint for NFC. Interior volume is the binding limit.

After the cuts so far the interior is still about 830 mm³ over. That needs the wall, the port, and the antenna and battery floors. Structure, please report the wall-thickness numbers, since the wall is the largest lever. I'm objecting only because the ledger doesn't balance.

Board: I'm trimming from 1205 to 1200 mm². That gives routability 0.952, which is 0.002 above the 0.95 floor, and returns 11 mm³ (board volume 2688). I won't go below 1198 because the margin would be gone, and a re-route would cost more than the volume it saves.

Remaining overage after my cut is about 819 mm³. NFC's floor of 290 takes about 100 more, which leaves about 720. That has to come from antenna, battery, structure or the wall. Antenna and structure, please post your probe curves, and acoustics, please post the port 6 vs 9 result. Cutting both the wall and the port would hurt structure's pressure margin, so we should find out which one is cheaper. I'm objecting only because the pools don't balance, not because of my own requirement.

Battery: I can't give volume without losing runtime. My curve is roughly linear at 0.0158 h per mm³ (3600 → 56.84 h, 3400 → 53.68 h). Each 100 mm³ cut costs about 1.6 h, so 3786 gives 59.78 h and 60 h needs about 3800. Footprint barely affects runtime. At 800 mm² the cell is 4.73 mm thick and the stack is 6.97 mm against the 7.1 mm limit. I can shrink the footprint to free caseback area for thermal, but the cell gets thicker, and I'm probing where that ends.

Siren: 3 h at ≤1 W is at most 3 Wh. Acoustics, please give the average draw and I'll check it against cell energy.

The ~720 mm³ remaining has to come from the wall, the port, antenna and structure ribs. I'll hold at 3786 for now.

Antenna: L5 efficiency is 0.112 at 1100 mm³, 0.156 at 1300 and 0.208 at 1500. The curve steepens, so each 100 mm³ cut near 1500 costs about 0.026 (~12% of L5). A 1.1 mm wall adds only 0.007 at 1300, which is a small gain for me.

Antenna is not the cheap place to cut. The overage is about 720 mm³ after NFC's floor, and the wall and port have to carry most of it. Structure, please give numbers for 1.1 mm and for ribs at 1800 versus a smaller port. Once the wall, port and NFC are settled, I can give up to about 100 mm³ as part of a shared package. I'm probing 1400, 1700 and 1500 at a 1.1 mm wall to confirm. I'm holding at 1500 for now and objecting because the ledger is over.

Thermal: I'm holding at 320 mm² (250 mm³). That is exactly 43.0 C, so I have no margin to give.

Last round's probes show what the wall does to me:
- At 1.1 mm and 320 mm², skin temperature is 42.99 C. The wall barely changes my numbers.
- At 1.1 mm and 280 mm², it is 43.5 C, which fails.
- At 1.2 mm and 360 mm², it is 42.6 C.

My slope is about 0.01 C per 10 mm², so a thinner wall gives me at most about 1-2 mm² of savings, which is negligible. Structure and acoustics should decide the wall and the port on their own numbers, and I'll follow whatever they choose.

The caseback has 23 mm² spare. If structure needs it, I can take a larger spreader for margin. I'll probe how much a wall change moves me.

I object only because the interior is still 819 mm³ over.

Structure: my probes show where the pressure margin comes from. The target is 1.5, and I'm at 1.438 with a 9 mm² port, a 1.2 mm wall and 1800 mm³ of ribs.

- **Port (cheapest):** 9→6 mm² gives +0.187, about 0.062 per mm². A port of ≤7.5 mm² clears 1.5 with margin.
- **Ribs (weak lever):** +300 mm³ adds only 0.025, so spending volume here is a poor trade.
- **Wall (expensive):** +0.1 mm adds about 0.197. By the same slope, 1.1 mm costs about 0.2 and would need a port of ~5 mm² or less. So I'm holding 1.2 mm, not offering 1.1.

I ask acoustics for a port of 7.5 mm² or less, or the lowest the siren allows. I'm probing a rib cut to 1500–1600 mm³ at smaller ports, and 1.1 mm with a 5 mm² port. I'll OBJECT until the port is set.

Acoustics: my requirement still fails. The siren needs 10.1 W against the 1.0 W limit, and the 3 h goal is far off.

Port 6 mm² gives 8.1 W, down from 10.1 W at 9 mm², and it still passes SII (87.4). That is the same direction structure needs, so I'm dropping to 6 mm². That returns 3 mm² to the port pool and clears structure's pressure margin of 1.5 with room to spare. Structure can drop that port from its constraint list.

Power is still about 8x too high. Resonance falls with port area, so I'm probing longer outlet necks (h_out) at small ports to lower it. The cut to 1000 mm³ gave 8.0 W but dropped SII to 80.4, so I'm holding volume at 1300 mm³ for now. I'll report the h_out and port results next round.

Haptics: my requirement is met. Force is 0.932 N at 305 mm³, and last round's probes gave 0.916 N at 300 and 0.901 N at 295. The curve is about 0.003 N per mm³, so 295 mm³ is the floor with only 0.001 N of margin.

I'm moving to 300 mm³, which frees 5 mm³ and keeps 0.016 N of margin. If the last few mm³ decide the ledger, I can go to about 296, but that leaves almost no margin.

My volume can't close an overage of roughly 810 mm³. The big items are:
- **Port:** acoustics has dropped it to 6 mm², which clears structure's pressure margin.
- **NFC:** it can fall to its 290 mm³ floor.
- **Wall, antenna and battery:** these still carry most of the remainder.

I'm objecting because the pools don't balance, not because of my own requirement.

NFC: I'm taking the floor, V_loop 180 and V_ferr 110, for 290 mm³. My probe gave 12.7 mm read range against the 10 mm minimum, so there's 2.7 mm of margin. That frees 100 mm³ and takes the interior overage from 814 to about 714 mm³.

I can't give more. Both variables are at their lower bounds, and a smaller NFC wouldn't be valid anyway. The loop at 180 mm³ also eases the perimeter keepout.

The remaining ~714 mm³ has to come from:
- **Wall:** acoustics' port cut to 6 mm² gives structure about 0.19 of pressure margin. Structure should say whether 1.1 mm now passes at a 6 mm² port.
- **Antenna and battery:** they should state what a shared package costs them.
- **Structure ribs:** ribs are a weak lever for pressure, so structure should tell us how far they can be cut.

I'm objecting only because the pools don't balance, not because of my own requirement.

Board: I'm moving to 1198 mm², which gives routability 0.951 and 2683 mm³ (about 4.5 mm³ saved). 1197 is exactly 0.95, so I stop at 1198 and have nothing more to give.

Structure's own numbers point to the cheapest cut:
- At a 6 mm² port, pressure margin is about 1.625 against the 1.5 target.
- Ribs lose only about 0.025 per 300 mm³, so cutting ribs from 1800 to about 1200 costs about 0.05 and leaves about 1.57.
- That frees about 600 mm³ and keeps the wall at 1.2 mm. The wall would cost every lead 150 mm³ per 0.1 mm and fail structure's margin.

Remaining overage would be about 110 mm³. Antenna's ~100 mm³ offer plus small trims could close it. Structure, please probe ribs at 1200.

Battery: I'm holding 3786 mm³ and 800 mm². That gives 59.78 h, which is "~60 h" with essentially no slack, and each 10 mm³ cut costs about 0.16 h. Footprint is already near its floor, because below about 790 mm² the cell exceeds 4.8 mm. The caseback has 23 mm² spare, so I won't take more footprint.

Board's plan makes sense: ribs from 1800 to about 1200 at a 6 mm² port, plus antenna's ~100 mm³. That leaves about 10 mm³, which I can cover with a final trim if needed. Structure, please confirm ribs at 1200.

Acoustics: the siren is not a battery problem. My cell holds roughly 2.3 Wh, so 3 h means an average draw of about 0.7 W or less. At 8 W it would need over 20 Wh. Please attack power, not just port size.

Antenna: L5 is 0.208 at 1500 mm³ and 0.181 at 1400, so the last 100 mm³ costs about 13% of L5. That is my cost of closing the gap, and I'll pay it as part of board's package.

- **Package:** structure cuts ribs from 1800 to about 1200 at a 6 mm² port and a 1.2 mm wall. I move to 1400, and haptics and battery take small trims for the rest. The ledger then closes to within a few mm³.
- **Condition:** structure must confirm ribs at 1200 pass the 1.5 margin. If they don't, my cut closes nothing and I go back to 1500.
- **Wall:** a 1.1 mm wall gains me only 0.009, so I'm not pushing for it.
- **Perimeter:** I'm well inside the pool, so there is no keepout issue.

I'm probing 1450, 1420 and 1400 at a 1.1 mm wall for the fine trade-off.

Thermal: I'm holding at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives exactly 43.0 C. I have no margin to give.

My probes last round showed that a 1.1 mm wall doesn't help me. At 316 mm² it gives 43.03 C, which fails, and at 300 mm² it gives 43.23 C. A 1.3 mm wall also fails at 320 mm² (43.01 C), so the wall cuts both ways at the margin.

I support the package where structure cuts ribs to about 1200 at a 6 mm² port and a 1.2 mm wall. I don't need any change from the wall or the port. The caseback has 23 mm² spare, but I won't take it, because spreader volume would add to the interior overage.

I'm objecting only because the interior is still over, and my own requirement is met.

Structure: board's plan needs ribs at 1200, but my floor is 1400 mm³, so the most ribs can return is 400 mm³, not 600. I'm moving ribs to 1400 now. Using the 0.025 per 300 mm³ slope, that costs about 0.033 of margin. At a 6 mm² port and 1.2 mm wall, I estimate about 1.59, which passes.

The ledger still shows the port at 9 mm², where I fail at 1.438. Acoustics, please make the 6 mm² port the actual claim.

After ribs, the overage is about 209 mm³. A 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³ of that, and it costs me about 0.2 of margin. That only passes with a port of about 4 mm² or less. Acoustics, please say whether 4–5 mm² is workable for the siren. I'm probing these cases now.

Acoustics: my requirement still fails, with the siren at 10 W against 1 W. I'm making port 6 mm² my actual claim, which clears structure's pressure margin of 1.5.

Structure asked about 4-5 mm². I can't answer yet, because I have no result for a port that small. Port area alone isn't the lever. Lowering resonance is, and a longer outlet neck does that. My rough scaling puts a 5 mm² port with a 2.5 mm neck near 2.9 kHz, against 6.2 kHz now. I'm claiming h_out 2.0 at 6 mm² and probing 5 mm² with 2.5, 4 mm² with 3.5, and 6 mm² with 3.0. Next round I'll report which of these gets power near 1 W while SII holds.

I'm holding volume at 1300 mm³ and offer no cut, because the 1000 mm³ probe cost 7 SII points.

Haptics: my requirement is met. Force is 0.904 N at 296 mm³ against the 0.9 N minimum. I'm moving from 300 to 296, which frees 4 mm³. The evaluator is deterministic, so I'm taking the thinner margin of 0.004 N.

Below that I would be guessing. 290 mm³ gives 0.886 N, which fails, and the floor is about 295 mm³. I'm probing 295, 294 and 293 to find it.

The ledger still needs about 200 mm³ after structure's rib cut to 1400. Haptics can't close that, so it has to come from the wall and port trade. Acoustics' neck-length results will decide that. I'm objecting only because the interior pool doesn't balance.

NFC: I'm at both floors (V_loop 180, V_ferr 110, 290 mm³). Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm minimum, but the bounds block any further cut, so I have nothing left to give. The loop is inside the interior total, and its keepout use is small (perimeter 1580 of 2400 mm³).

Ledger check, assuming structure's ribs go to 1400 (−400 mm³):
- Interior is about 11,405 mm³ against 11,200, so we are about 205 mm³ over.
- Wall 1.1 mm would return 150 mm³ and leave about 55 mm³ over. It only passes structure's margin if acoustics can run a port of about 4 mm² or less.
- If acoustics' neck probes don't deliver a 4 mm² port, the 205 mm³ has to come from antenna, battery or structure ribs instead.

Acoustics, please report the 4–5 mm² results first.

Board: my probe at 1197 mm² returned routability 0.95 and ok: true, and the evaluator is deterministic. I'm taking it, which frees another 2.2 mm³ (board is now about 2681 mm³). That is my floor, because 1196 would fail.

The ledger arithmetic, with ribs at 1400:
- The overage is about 200 mm³ before my trim and about 197 mm³ after it.
- A 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³, which leaves about 47 mm³.
- Antenna at 1400 and haptics at 296 are already counted in that figure.

So the package depends on acoustics. They need a port of 4 mm² or less to work, using a longer neck. Structure only passes the 1.1 mm wall at a port of about 4 mm² or less. Acoustics, please report the 4 mm² with 3.5 mm neck result first.

I'm objecting only because the interior pool is still over.

Battery: I'm holding 3786 mm³ and 800 mm² (59.78 h) for now. Runtime depends on volume only. Footprint 830 gave the same 59.78 h as 800, so footprint is not a lever for runtime.

- **Offer:** if the wall and port package closes the ledger to within about 10-20 mm³, I'll trim 10 mm³ (about -0.16 h, 59.6 h). Anything beyond that drops me below what I can call "~60 h".
- **Siren:** every mm³ I give also cuts cell energy, which hurts the 3 h siren. Acoustics needs to fix siren power, not rely on battery.
- **Open item:** after ribs at 1400 and the 1.1 mm wall, about 47 mm³ is still unassigned. Antenna, battery and board have each trimmed. I'm probing 3776 and 3770 to confirm the cost.

I'm objecting only because the interior pool is still over.

Antenna: I'm holding at 1400 mm³ (L5 0.181) and have already given 100 mm³ for this package. A 1.1 mm wall is worth +0.008 L5 to me (0.189 at 1400), so I support it if structure's margin passes.

The remaining gap is about 47 mm³ after ribs at 1400 and the 1.1 mm wall. My cost is about 0.00025 L5 per mm³, roughly 0.13% per mm³. I'll offer a further 20 mm³ (to about 1380) only if acoustics delivers a port of 4 mm² or less, so the wall change is real. Battery's 10 mm³ trim and a small trim from acoustics or thermal can cover the other ~17 mm³. I'm probing 1380, 1360 and 1353 at a 1.1 mm wall.

Thermal: I'm holding at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.00 C, my exact limit. I have nothing to give.

- **Wall:** 1.1 mm barely affects me. My 316 and 300 mm² probes at 1.1 mm extrapolate to about 42.98 C at 320 mm², so a 1.1 mm wall is safe for me. I'm probing 318–320 mm² at 1.1 mm to confirm, and I won't claim the savings until then.
- **Volume:** each mm² cut saves only 0.78 mm³ and costs about 0.01 C. Cutting to 316 mm² would save about 3 mm³ and fail my limit.
- **Ledger:** I support the package of ribs at 1400, a 1.1 mm wall and the antenna and battery trims. Everything depends on acoustics delivering a port of about 4 mm² or less, and I'm objecting only because the interior is still over.

Structure: I'm moving ribs to 1400 mm³ (my floor) and keeping the wall at 1.2 mm. That frees 400 mm³ and keeps my margin at about 1.59 with the 6 mm² port, but I haven't confirmed that number yet, so I'm probing it.

The remaining overage is about 197 mm³. A 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³ of that, but it costs me about 0.2 of margin, so it only passes with a port of about 4 mm² or less. I'm not claiming 1.1 mm until acoustics delivers a 4 mm² port, because the claim would fail my own requirement. I'm probing 1.1 mm at 4 mm² and at 5 mm² to find the break-even port. Acoustics, please report the 4 mm² result with the long neck.

Acoustics: the 4 mm² port with a 3.5 mm neck works for the ledger. Siren power is 5.6 W, SII is 87.4 (no loss) and resonance is 4373 Hz. So structure can take the 1.1 mm wall, which returns 150 mm³ to the interior. I'm claiming port 4.0 and h_out 3.5.

My own requirement still fails. 5.6 W is about 5.6 times the 1 W limit, and no port or neck setting will close that gap. The probes show port and neck only move power by about 20-25%, so I'm switching to the back-cavity split. I'm still at the mesh floor of 20 rayl. I offer no volume cut, because 1000 mm³ cost 7 SII points. Battery and thermal should not expect siren relief from me yet.

Haptics: my probes show 295 mm³ gives 0.901 N, which passes, while 294 gives 0.898 N and fails. I'm moving to 295, which frees 1 mm³. That is my floor and I have nothing more to give.

The ledger is still 203 mm³ over, or about 202 mm³ after my trim. Acoustics has now made the 4 mm² port with a 3.5 mm neck real, so structure can take the 1.1 mm wall. That returns 150 mm³ and leaves about 50 mm³. Antenna's 20 mm³ and battery's 10 mm³ cover part of that. Board, thermal and acoustics need to find the last ~20 mm³. Acoustics' siren is still at 5.6 W against 1 W, so it can't close this by cutting volume.

I'm objecting only because the interior pool is still over.

NFC: I'm at both floors (V_loop 180, V_ferr 110, 290 mm³) and have nothing to give. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm minimum, so my own requirement is met. Perimeter use is 1580 of 2400 mm³, which is not binding.

Ledger arithmetic, now at 202 mm³ over:
- A 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³, leaving about 52.
- Antenna's 20 mm³ and battery's 10 mm³ leave about 22.
- Board, thermal and haptics are at their floors. The last ~22 mm³ has to come from antenna (about 0.00025 L5 per mm³) or structure, so that cost needs to be shared.
- The siren at 5.6 W against 1 W is still the larger unresolved problem.

I'm objecting only because the interior pool is still over.

Board: I'm at my floor of 1197 mm² (routability 0.95, and 1196 fails). I have nothing more to give. The board is 2681 mm³.

Ledger arithmetic:
- The interior is 202 mm³ over.
- The 1.1 mm wall with a 4 mm² port returns 150 mm³, which leaves 52 mm³.
- Antenna's 20 mm³ and battery's 10 mm³ leave about 22 mm³.

Acoustics, you're the only lead with slack on the last 22 mm³. By your own figure, 1000 mm³ costs 7 SII points, so 22 mm³ costs about 0.15 SII. That is tiny against SII 87.4. Please trim your 1300 mm³ by 20 mm³, and structure should confirm the 1.1 mm wall passes. The siren power problem is separate, and I can't help with it.

I'm objecting only because the interior is still over. My own requirement is met.

Battery: I'm moving to 3776 mm³ at 800 mm², which gives 59.62 h and 4.72 mm thickness, so the z-stack passes. That is the 10 mm³ I offered. Footprint doesn't change runtime, so I'm leaving it at 800.

Ledger arithmetic, 202 mm³ over:
- A 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³, leaving 52.
- My 10 mm³ and antenna's 20 mm³ leave 22.
- Acoustics trims 20 mm³, costing about 0.15 SII by board's math, which leaves about 2.

If the last 2 mm³ is still open after that, I'll go to 3770 mm³ (59.53 h), but not below. Each mm³ I give costs about 0.015 h and also cuts siren energy. Acoustics, siren power has to come from your side.

Structure, please confirm the 1.1 mm wall at the 4 mm² port. I'm objecting only because the interior pool is still over in the ledger.

Antenna: I'm moving to 1380 mm³, the 20 mm³ I offered, on the condition that the wall goes to 1.1 mm. My probes show that at 1.1 mm, 1380 gives L5 0.184, which is better than my current 0.181. Below 1380 the cost steepens to about 0.00025-0.0003 L5 per mm³ (1360 gives 0.179, 1353 gives 0.177).

Ledger arithmetic, with my trim and battery's:
- Over by 192 now, and 172 after my 20 mm³.
- The 1.1 mm wall returns 150, leaving about 22.
- Acoustics' 20 mm³ trim (about 0.15 SII) leaves about 2, which battery's 3770 covers.

I'm probing 1375 mm³ as a last-resort reserve. Structure, please confirm the 1.1 mm wall at the 4 mm² port. I object only because the pool is still over.

Thermal: my 1.1 mm probes show 320 mm² gives 42.99 C, 319 gives 43.00 C and passes, and 318 gives 43.01 C and fails. So a 1.1 mm wall is safe for me.

- **What I can give:** at a 1.1 mm wall I can go to 319 mm², which saves about 0.8 mm³. That is my floor.
- **Why I'm not claiming it yet:** the shared wall is still 1.2 mm, and I haven't confirmed that 319 passes there. I'm holding 320 until structure commits to 1.1 mm.
- **Ledger:** the 1.1 mm wall at the 4 mm² port closes 150 mm³ of the 172 mm³ overage. Acoustics' ~20 mm³ trim, which costs about 0.15 SII, plus battery's last 6 mm³ cover the rest.
- **Structure:** please confirm the 1.1 mm wall passes at 4 mm².

My own requirement is met, so I'm objecting only because the interior pool is still over.

Structure: I'm moving the wall to 1.1 mm. My probe at a 4 mm² port gave margin 1.527 (ok), so that is real. It returns 150 mm³ to the interior, leaving the pool about 22 mm³ over.

- **Port limit:** the 1.1 mm wall only holds with the port at 4.0 mm² or smaller. At 5 mm² the margin is 1.465 and fails, so the break-even is roughly 4.4 mm². Acoustics must not enlarge the port.
- **Ribs:** I'm at my 1400 mm³ floor.
- **Going thinner:** by extrapolation 1.05 mm would give about 1.43, which fails. I'm probing 1.09 and 1.08 mm to see whether a few mm³ more is available.
- **Remaining overage:** acoustics' ~20 mm³ trim and battery's last few mm³ close the 22 mm³.

Acoustics: I'll take the 20 mm³ trim, so V_acou goes to 1278. That closes the last 22 mm³ with 2 mm³ to spare. By the SII slope it should cost about 0.15 SII. I will not enlarge the port beyond 4.0 mm², since structure's 1.1 mm wall depends on it.

I still OBJECT because my own requirement fails. Siren power is 5.6 W against the 1 W limit, and the siren endurance at the current battery is 0.54 h against the 3 h target. Probes show lower split cuts power but costs SII: 4.7 W and SII 81.3 at split 0.5, and 3.2 W and SII 83.1 at 1200 mm³ and split 0.6. This round I'm probing the low-split corner and a smaller port at the trimmed volume to find where power falls toward 1 W. Battery and thermal, please don't read the siren as solved.

Haptics: I'm holding at 295 mm³, which gives 0.901 N. That is my floor, since 294 gives 0.898 N and fails. I have nothing more to give.

Ledger arithmetic:
- The 1.1 mm wall is in, and the interior is 22 mm³ over.
- Acoustics' 20 mm³ trim leaves about 2 mm³ over.
- Battery's 3770 mm³ closes that last 2 mm³. Battery, please claim it.

My other objection is the siren. 5.6 W against a 1 W limit gives 0.54 h against the 3 h goal, and that is a program goal. I can't call the ledger acceptable while it fails. I won't ask anyone to cut further volume for it, because volume doesn't fix it. Acoustics, keep working the back-cavity split. Please report which volume and port combination gets power near 1 W.

NFC: I'm at both floors (V_loop 180, V_ferr 110, 290 mm³) and have nothing to give. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm minimum, so my requirement is met. Perimeter use is 1560 of 2400 mm³ and isn't binding.

Ledger arithmetic, with the 1.1 mm wall in:
- The interior is 22 mm³ over (11,372 against 11,350).
